aorta-systemic-trunk.title: Aorta & Great Systemic Arterial Trunk
aorta-systemic-trunk.description: The largest systemic artery in the human body, arising from the left ventricle and distributing oxygenated blood under pulsatile systolic pressure.
aorta-systemic-trunk.body:
# Aorta & Great Systemic Arterial Trunk

The aorta is the prime systemic conduit delivering oxygenated blood from the left ventricle. Its high concentration of elastic fibers allows it to expand during systolic ejection and recoil during diastole (Windkessel effect), ensuring continuous peripheral perfusion.

cardiac-chambers.title: The Four Cardiac Chambers & Valvular System
cardiac-chambers.description: Morphological and functional specialization of the right and left atria and ventricles, partitioned by the interventricular septum and unidirectional atrioventricular/semilunar valves.

misconceptions.claim: The left and right ventricles pump different volumes of blood per beat.
misconceptions.correction: Both ventricles pump the exact same stroke volume (~70 mL per beat); only the systolic pressure generated differs (~120 mmHg in Left Ventricle vs ~25 mmHg in Right Ventricle).

cardiac-chambers.body:
# The Four Cardiac Chambers & Valvular System

The human heart is divided by muscular and fibrous septa into four distinct chambers:
1. **Right Atrium (RA)**: Receives systemic venous return via Superior Vena Cava (SVC) and Inferior Vena Cava (IVC).
2. **Right Ventricle (RV)**: Pumps into Pulmonary Trunk through the Pulmonary Semilunar Valve.
3. **Left Atrium (LA)**: Receives 4 Pulmonary Veins (2 left, 2 right).
4. **Left Ventricle (LV)**: High-pressure conical chamber pumping into the Aorta through the Aortic Semilunar Valve.

digestive-system.title: Human Alimentary Canal & Digestive System
digestive-system.description: Gastrointestinal organ system responsible for mechanical mastication, enzymatic hydrolysis, nutrient absorption, and waste excretion.
digestive-system.body:
# Human Alimentary Canal & Digestive System

The human alimentary canal is a continuous muscular tube spanning approximately $9\text{ meters}$ extending from the buccal cavity to the anus, accompanied by specialized accessory digestive glands (salivary glands, liver with gallbladder, and pancreas).

flower-anatomy.title: Longitudinal Section of a Bisexual Flower
flower-anatomy.description: Structural morphology of angiosperm reproductive organs detailing sepals, petals, stamen (filament and anther with pollen), and carpel/pistil (stigma, style, ovary with ovules).

equations.meaning: Syngamy and sexual reproduction in flowering plants.

flower-anatomy.body:
# Flower Anatomy

Figure 7.7 in NCERT Class 10 Biology illustrates the reproductive architecture of angiosperms. Students are assessed on identifying male vs female organs, explaining self-pollination vs cross-pollination, and tracing post-fertilization changes (ovule becomes seed, ovary wall becomes pericarp/fruit).

human-excretory-system.title: Human Excretory (Urinary) System
human-excretory-system.description: Biological organ system comprising paired kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, and urethra for removing nitrogenous metabolic waste products (urea, uric acid) from blood circulation.

equations.meaning: Renal clearance and urine formation pathway.

human-excretory-system.body:
# Human Excretory System

NCERT Class 10 Chapter 5 outlines the filtration of blood and elimination of toxic nitrogenous metabolites. The anatomical architecture coordinates high-pressure renal arterial perfusion with tubular reabsorption to maintain homeostatic osmotic balance.

human-eye-optics.title: The Human Eye as an Optical Instrument
human-eye-optics.description: Biological photoreceptive organ utilizing a curved cornea, iris diaphragm, crystalline lens, and retina to focus light into visual neural impulses.

sources.name: NCERT Class 10 Science
sources.chapter: Chapter 11: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
sources.section: 11.1 The Human Eye and Power of Accommodation

misconceptions.claim: The eye lens provides the vast majority of refraction.
misconceptions.correction: Most refraction occurs at the outer air-cornea interface (~43 dioptres); the crystalline lens fine-tunes focal accommodation (~15–20 dioptres).

human-eye-optics.body:
# The Human Eye as an Optical Instrument

The human eyeball is approximately spherical with a diameter of about $2.3\text{ cm}$. Light entering through the protective transparent cornea passes through the aqueous humor, pupil aperture, crystalline lens, and vitreous body to cast a real, inverted image onto the neuro-retinal membrane.

human-heart-circulation.title: Double Circulation in the Human Heart
human-heart-circulation.description: Closed dual-circuit cardiovascular system consisting of a low-pressure pulmonary loop to the lungs and a high-pressure systemic loop to the body organs.

sources.name: NCERT Class 10 Science
sources.section: 6.4.1 Transportation in Human Beings — Our Pump: The Heart

misconceptions.claim: All arteries always carry oxygen-rich blood, and all veins carry carbon-dioxide-rich blood.
misconceptions.correction: Exception: The Pulmonary Artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs, while the Pulmonary Veins carry oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.

misconceptions.claim: The right and left sides of the heart contract at completely separate times.
misconceptions.correction: Both atria contract simultaneously (atrial systole) while ventricles relax (ventricular diastole), followed by simultaneous contraction of both ventricles (ventricular systole).

human-heart-circulation.body:
# Double Circulation in the Human Heart

## 1. Physiological Mechanism
Human circulation is termed *double circulation* because blood passes through the four-chambered heart twice in one complete cardiovascular transit:
1. **Pulmonary Circulation**: Transports deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle through the pulmonary arteries to the lung alveoli for gaseous exchange ($\text{CO}_2$ release, $\text{O}_2$ uptake), and returns oxygenated blood through the pulmonary veins into the left atrium.
2. **Systemic Circulation**: Transports oxygenated blood from the muscular left ventricle through the aorta to all capillary beds in systemic tissues and organs, returning oxygen-depleted blood via the superior and inferior vena cava into the right atrium.

human-respiratory-system.title: Human Respiratory System & Alveoli
human-respiratory-system.description: Anatomical organ system responsible for pulmonary ventilation, external respiration, and gaseous exchange of O2 and CO2 across the alveolar-capillary membrane.

equations.meaning: Aerobic cellular respiration utilizing pulmonary oxygen.

human-respiratory-system.body:
# Human Respiratory System

The respiratory system in NCERT Class 10 Biology explains human aerobic metabolism. Students are frequently tested on the anatomical pathway of air, the physiological function of cartilage rings, and how the alveolar architecture maximizes diffusion surface area.

nephron.title: Nephron (Microscopic Kidney Filtration Unit)
nephron.description: The structural and functional unit of the vertebrate kidney comprising a glomerulus, Bowman's capsule, convoluted tubules, and Loop of Henle for selective filtration and reabsorption.

equations.latex: \\text{Urine Volume} = \\text{Glomerular Filtration (180 L)} - \\text{Tubular Reabsorption (178.5 L)} \\approx 1.5\\text{ L/day}
equations.meaning: Selective tubular conservation of fluid and solutes in the nephron.

nephron.body:
# Nephron Structure and Function

The nephron is the centerpiece of renal physiology in CBSE Class 10. The three phases of urine formation—Ultrafiltration at the glomerulus, Selective Reabsorption along the renal tubule, and Tubular Secretion—are directly represented in this 3D model.

reflex-arc.title: Somatic Reflex Arc Neural Circuit
reflex-arc.description: Neural wiring diagram and pathway that mediates an involuntary, rapid, automatic response to a dangerous sensory stimulus without prior conscious brain intervention.

equations.meaning: Unbroken physiological reflex arc sequence.

reflex-arc.body:
# Reflex Arc

Reflex arcs evolved as an efficient emergency response system in animals. In CBSE Class 10 examinations, students are required to trace the complete circuit from peripheral receptor to muscle effector and explain why the spinal cord executes the motor withdrawal before the brain consciously registers the sensation of heat or pain.

stoma.title: Stomatal Apparatus & Guard Cell Mechanism
stoma.description: Specialized microscopic leaf epidermal structure consisting of paired guard cells controlling the stomatal aperture for photosynthetic gas exchange and transpiration.

equations.latex: \\text{Endosmosis} \\rightarrow \\text{Guard cells turgid} \\rightarrow \\text{Stoma opens}; \\quad \\text{Exosmosis} \\rightarrow \\text{Guard cells flaccid} \\rightarrow \\text{Stoma closes}
equations.meaning: Turgor pressure regulation of stomatal pore aperture.

stoma.body:
# Stomatal Apparatus

In NCERT Class 10 Biology, the stomatal apparatus illustrates how cellular turgor mechanics regulate macroscopic physiological processes. The differential thickness between inner and outer cell walls is the mechanical basis for opening and closing.

trophic-level-pyramid.title: Ecological Trophic Pyramid & 10% Energy Transfer Law
trophic-level-pyramid.description: Stepped ecological model illustrating the unidirectional trophic energy hierarchy from primary producers to apex predators, governed by Lindeman's 10% law and biomagnification.

equations.meaning: Lindeman's 10 percent energy transfer rule between consecutive trophic tiers.
Trophic energy attenuation sequence.

trophic-level-pyramid.body:
# Ecological Trophic Pyramid

Chapter 13 in NCERT Class 10 explores trophic ecology. The step pyramid geometry visually enforces the dual core principles: the rapid attenuation of usable metabolic energy (10% law) and the catastrophic reciprocal concentration of environmental contaminants (biomagnification) at the top of the food chain.

bunsen-burner.title: Laboratory Bunsen Burner
bunsen-burner.description: Standard gas-fueled laboratory apparatus delivering an adjustable oxidizing or reducing flame for heating and combustion reactions.

sources.name: NCERT Laboratory Manual for Class 10 Science

equations.meaning: Complete combustion of methane fuel with open collar in blue non-luminous flame.

safety: Always light match before opening the gas valve.
Use blue non-luminous flame for clean heating without soot deposits.
bunsen-burner.body:
# Laboratory Bunsen Burner

## Anatomy & Operation
The Bunsen burner comprises a heavy cast-iron base, a vertical brass barrel, a needle gas jet, and an adjustable rotating air collar. Adjusting the air collar controls air-fuel stoichiometry between a sooty yellow flame ($300^\circ\text{C}$) and a clean, high-temperature blue oxidizing flame ($1100^\circ\text{C}$).

combination-reaction.title: Combination Reaction (Synthesis Reaction)
combination-reaction.description: Chemical reaction type where two or more reactants combine to form a single product.

equations.meaning: Two distinct elemental or compound reactants join to produce a single unified product compound.

combination-reaction.body:
# Combination Reaction

A reaction in which a single product is formed from two or more reactants is known as a combination reaction.
In the burning of magnesium ribbon:
$$2\text{Mg}(s) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{MgO}(s)$$
Elemental magnesium and molecular oxygen combine into a single substance, solid magnesium oxide.

crucible-tongs.title: Crucible & Laboratory Tongs
crucible-tongs.description: Scissor-style stainless steel gripping apparatus designed for safely holding hot crucibles, evaporating dishes, and magnesium strips.

sources.name: NCERT Laboratory Manual for Class 10 Science

safety: Ensure serrated gripping tips have firm mechanical traction on the object before lifting.
Never touch hot metal ends with bare hands even after removing from flame.
crucible-tongs.body:
# Crucible & Laboratory Tongs

Stainless steel laboratory tongs with bowed serrated jaws and looped handles designed to manipulate hot experimental vessels and combustible metal strips at safe operator distance.

diamond-lattice.title: Diamond Allotrope 3D Tetrahedral Crystal Lattice
diamond-lattice.description: Structural allotrope of carbon wherein every carbon atom is tetrahedrally bonded to four others via rigid covalent bonds, resulting in exceptional hardness and high melting temperature.

equations.meaning: Allotropic structural form of carbon in diamond.

diamond-lattice.body:
# Diamond Allotrope

Diamond represents carbon in its densest crystalline configuration. The isotropic distribution of tetrahedral single covalent bonds in all three dimensions eliminates any natural cleavage planes, creating extreme resistance to mechanical deformation.

displacement-reaction.title: Single Displacement Reaction (Iron in Copper Sulphate)
displacement-reaction.description: Canonical CBSE Class 10 chemistry experiment demonstrating that a more reactive metal (iron) displaces a less reactive metal (copper) from its aqueous salt solution.

equations.meaning: Single displacement of copper by iron forming iron(II) sulphate and copper metal.

displacement-reaction.body:
# Single Displacement Reaction

Activity 1.9 of NCERT Class 10 demonstrates chemical reactivity and redox electron exchange. Iron atoms lose electrons to form $Fe^{2+}$ ions that dissolve into solution, while $Cu^{2+}$ ions from the blue solution accept electrons to plate onto the iron surface as reddish-brown elemental copper.

graphite-lattice.title: Graphite Allotrope Layered Hexagonal Lattice
graphite-lattice.description: Planar allotrope of carbon consisting of two-dimensional hexagonal carbon rings arranged in parallel layers held by weak van der Waals forces, enabling electrical conduction and lubricity.

equations.meaning: Electronic structure of graphite accounting for planar conductivity.

graphite-lattice.body:
# Graphite Allotrope

Graphite is the thermodynamically standard state of carbon. The anisotropy between strong in-plane covalent bonding and weak out-of-plane van der Waals forces gives graphite its distinctive electrical conductivity and lubricative properties.

hydrogen-evolution.title: Reaction of Granulated Zinc with Acid & H2 Evolution
hydrogen-evolution.description: Classic CBSE Class 10 acid-base laboratory experiment demonstrating metal-acid single replacement to evolve hydrogen gas, tested via the characteristic pop sound.

sources.name: NCERT Class 10 Science
sources.section: 2.1.2 How do Acids and Bases React with Metals? (Activity 2.1)

equations.meaning: Reaction of zinc with dilute sulphuric acid producing zinc sulphate and hydrogen gas.
Combustion of hydrogen gas producing the diagnostic pop sound.

hydrogen-evolution.body:
# Reaction of Zinc with Dilute Acid

Activity 2.1 in NCERT Class 10 demonstrates the fundamental reaction between metals and acids: $\text{Acid} + \text{Metal} \rightarrow \text{Salt} + \text{Hydrogen gas}$. The pop sound confirms the flammable nature and presence of pure hydrogen gas.

magnesium-metal.title: Magnesium Metal (Mg, Atomic Number 12)
magnesium-metal.description: Highly reactive alkaline earth metal in Group 2 of the Periodic Table with electronic configuration 2, 8, 2.

equations.meaning: Electropositive magnesium atom donates two valence electrons during oxidation.

misconceptions.claim: Magnesium ribbon stored in the laboratory is 100% pure elemental magnesium at the surface.
misconceptions.correction: Atmospheric moisture and carbon dioxide form a thin protective layer of basic magnesium carbonate that must be abraded off with sandpaper.

magnesium-metal.body:
# Magnesium Metal (Mg)

## Electronic Structure & Reactivity
Magnesium ($Z = 12$) has 12 protons and 12 electrons configured as $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2$ (or $2, 8, 2$). 
With a low first and second ionization enthalpy, it acts as a strong reducing agent in combination and displacement reactions.

magnesium-oxide.title: Magnesium Oxide (MgO)
magnesium-oxide.description: White ionic solid compound composed of Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ ions in a face-centered cubic lattice; acts as a basic metallic oxide.

sources.name: NCERT Class 10 Science
sources.section: 2.1.5 Reaction of Metallic Oxides with Acids

equations.meaning: Magnesium oxide hydrolyzes into alkaline magnesium hydroxide solution.
Basic oxide neutralizes hydrochloric acid to yield magnesium chloride and water.

misconceptions.claim: All metal oxides are completely insoluble in water.
misconceptions.correction: While most are insoluble, oxides of metals like Mg dissolve slightly to produce alkaline solutions.

magnesium-oxide.body:
# Magnesium Oxide (MgO)

## Nature and Properties
Magnesium oxide is an odorless, non-toxic white powder possessing a high melting point ($2852^\circ\text{C}$), making it valuable as a refractory lining material. In CBSE Class 10 chemistry, it serves as the primary exemplar of basic metallic oxides.

## Crystal Structure and Unit Cell Accounting
Magnesium oxide crystallizes in the rock-salt (halite) structure, consisting of interpenetrating face-centered cubic (FCC) lattices of $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ cations and $\text{O}^{2-}$ anions:
- **Coordination Number**: Each $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ion is octahedrally coordinated by 6 $\text{O}^{2-}$ ions, and each $\text{O}^{2-}$ is coordinated by 6 $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ions (6:6 coordination).
- **Fractional Boundary Accounting per Conventional Unit Cell**:
  - $\text{O}^{2-}$ ions occupy FCC lattice points: $8 \text{ corners} \times \frac{1}{8} + 6 \text{ faces} \times \frac{1}{2} = 1 + 3 = 4\text{ ions}$.
  - $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ions occupy octahedral interstitial sites: $12 \text{ edges} \times \frac{1}{4} + 1 \text{ body centre} \times 1 = 3 + 1 = 4\text{ ions}$.
- **Net Unit Cell Composition**: Exactly 4 formula units of $\text{MgO}$ per conventional unit cell, preserving rigorous $1:1$ stoichiometric neutrality without double-counting shared boundary sites.

magnesium-ribbon-combustion.title: Combustion of Magnesium Ribbon in Air
magnesium-ribbon-combustion.description: Highly exothermic combination reaction where magnesium ribbon burns in atmospheric oxygen with a dazzling white flame to form magnesium oxide ash.

equations.meaning: Two moles of solid magnesium metal react with one mole of atmospheric oxygen gas upon heating to produce two moles of solid magnesium oxide powder along with substantial thermal and luminous energy.
Magnesium oxide reacts with water to form basic magnesium hydroxide, turning red litmus paper blue.

misconceptions.claim: The white powder left behind is unburnt magnesium or soot.
misconceptions.correction: The powder is a completely new chemical compound, magnesium oxide (MgO), with distinct physical and chemical properties.

misconceptions.claim: Magnesium catches fire immediately at room temperature.
misconceptions.correction: Magnesium requires initial activation energy provided by the Bunsen flame before the reaction becomes self-sustaining and exothermic.

safety: Wear UV-protective safety glasses or darkened goggles to prevent retinal glare and UV radiation damage.
Always hold the ribbon using steel crucible tongs at arm's length; never touch the burning strip.
Collect ash in a watch glass or porcelain crucible placed over a heat-resistant ceramic mat.
magnesium-ribbon-combustion.body:
# Combustion of Magnesium Ribbon in Air

## 1. Educational Overview
The burning of magnesium ribbon in air is the canonical foundational demonstration in the CBSE Class 10 Chemistry curriculum (NCERT Chapter 1, Activity 1.1). It introduces students to the observable hallmarks of a chemical reaction:
- Evolution of energy (heat and dazzling white light).
- Change in state and color (silvery flexible metal strip $\rightarrow$ brittle white powder).
- Formation of a new chemical substance with basic oxide properties.

## 2. Experimental Procedure
1. Take a 3–4 cm long strip of magnesium ribbon.
2. Clean its surface thoroughly by rubbing with sandpaper until the silvery metal shines.
3. Hold the cleaned ribbon securely with a pair of crucible tongs.
4. Heat the tip of the ribbon in the hottest oxidizing zone (blue outer cone) of a Bunsen burner flame.
5. As soon as the dazzling white ignition starts, hold the burning strip over a clean watch glass to collect the white magnesium oxide powder.

methane-molecule.title: Methane (CH4) Covalent Molecular Structure
methane-molecule.description: Fundamental hydrocarbon illustrating tetrahedral covalent bonding, four single covalent bonds, and sp3 electron sharing in carbon compounds.

sources.name: NCERT Class 10 Science
sources.section: 4.1 Bonding in Carbon — The Covalent Bond

equations.meaning: Formation of methane through mutual sharing of 4 electron pairs.

methane-molecule.body:
# Methane (CH4)

Methane is the foundational paradigm for covalent chemical bonding in CBSE Class 10 Chemistry. By sharing electrons rather than transferring them, carbon attains a stable octet while hydrogen attains a stable duplet.

oxygen-element.title: Oxygen Element & Diatomic Molecule (O, O₂)
oxygen-element.description: Highly electronegative non-metal in Group 16 of the Periodic Table with electronic configuration 2, 6; acts as the primary oxidizing agent in combustion reactions.

sources.name: NCERT Class 10 Science
sources.section: 3.2.1 What happens when Metals are burnt in Air?

equations.meaning: Oxygen atom gains two electrons to form the divalent oxide anion.
Thermal dissociation of covalent oxygen molecules in combustion flame.

misconceptions.claim: Oxygen itself burns during combustion reactions.
misconceptions.correction: Oxygen is a supporter of combustion and an oxidizing agent; it does not burn on its own.

oxygen-element.body:
# Oxygen Element (O, Z=8)

## Electronic Structure & Chemical Behavior
Oxygen ($Z = 8$) has 8 protons and 8 electrons configured as $1s^2 2s^2 2p^4$ (or $[2, 6]$). 
With high electronegativity (3.44 on the Pauling scale), it readily pulls valence electrons from electropositive metals such as magnesium, forming crystalline basic oxides.

soap-micelle.title: Soap Micelle & Cleansing Mechanism
soap-micelle.description: Spherical colloidal aggregate of amphiphilic soap molecules trapping grease droplets in water to form a stable washable emulsion.

equations.meaning: Amphiphilic dissociation of sodium stearate soap molecule.

soap-micelle.body:
# Soap Micelle

Section 4.3.4 of NCERT Class 10 explores the physical chemistry of cleansing action. Oily dirt is insoluble in pure water, but becomes solubilized when surrounded by the hydrocarbon tails of soap molecules inside the core of a micelle.

tripod-wire-gauze.title: Tripod Stand with Wire Gauze & Porcelain Dish
tripod-wire-gauze.description: Standard laboratory heating platform for even heat distribution from a Bunsen burner to delicate glassware or evaporating dishes.

equations.meaning: Oxidation of copper to black copper(II) oxide on heating.
Reduction of copper(II) oxide back to copper metal by hydrogen.

tripod-wire-gauze.body:
# Tripod Stand and Wire Gauze

The tripod stand and ceramic-centered wire gauze constitute the fundamental heating station in chemistry laboratories, providing a stable, thermally buffered platform for reactions such as the oxidation and reduction of copper in CBSE Class 10 Activity 1.11.

water-electrolysis.title: Electrolytic Decomposition of Water
water-electrolysis.description: Standard CBSE Class 10 chemistry experiment demonstrating the decomposition of water into hydrogen and oxygen gases in a 2:1 stoichiometric volume ratio using electric current.

equations.meaning: Balanced chemical equation for electrolytic decomposition of water.

water-electrolysis.body:
# Electrolysis of Water

Activity 1.7 in NCERT Class 10 Chemistry proves the chemical composition of water through electrical energy. The 2:1 volume ratio observed between the cathode and anode gas collections provides empirical proof that water consists of hydrogen and oxygen in a 2:1 atomic proportion.

cbse-class-10-science.title: CBSE Class 10 Science (Board Examination Framework)
cbse-class-10-science.description: Official national curriculum standard published by CBSE and NCERT for secondary science education across Chemical Substances, World of Living, and Natural Phenomena.
cbse-class-10-science.body:
# CBSE Class 10 Science Curriculum Specification

The CBSE Class 10 Science course (Code 086) establishes foundational STEM literacy organized into five thematic units:
1. **Unit I: Chemical Substances — Nature and Behaviour** (Chemical Reactions, Acids/Bases/Salts, Metals and Non-Metals, Carbon Compounds).
2. **Unit II: World of Living** (Life Processes, Control and Coordination, Reproduction, Heredity).
3. **Unit III: Natural Phenomena** (Light – Reflection and Refraction, The Human Eye and Colourful World).
4. **Unit IV: Effects of Current** (Electricity, Magnetic Effects of Electric Current).
5. **Unit V: Natural Resources** (Our Environment).

ncert-biology-ch06.title: NCERT Class 10 Biology — Chapter 6: Life Processes
ncert-biology-ch06.description: Curriculum mapping for nutrition, respiration, transportation in animals and plants, and excretory systems.
ncert-biology-ch06.body:
# NCERT Class 10 Biology Chapter 6: Life Processes

Comprehensive study of metabolic life-sustaining processes: Autotrophic & Heterotrophic Nutrition, Aerobic & Anaerobic Respiration, Double Circulation & Lymphatic System, and Human Excretory System (Nephron structure).

ncert-chemistry-ch01.title: NCERT Class 10 Chemistry — Chapter 1: Chemical Reactions and Equations
ncert-chemistry-ch01.description: Curriculum mapping for chemical equations, balancing by hit-and-trial, combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement, oxidation, and reduction reactions.
ncert-chemistry-ch01.body:
# NCERT Class 10 Chemistry Chapter 1

## Core Activities & Practical Demonstrations
- **Activity 1.1**: Burning of Magnesium Ribbon in Air ($2\text{Mg} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MgO}$).
- **Activity 1.2**: Precipitation of Lead Iodide ($\text{Pb(NO}_3)_2 + 2\text{KI} \rightarrow \text{PbI}_2 \downarrow + 2\text{KNO}_3$).
- **Activity 1.3**: Zinc Granules in Dilute Sulphuric Acid ($\text{Zn} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{ZnSO}_4 + \text{H}_2 \uparrow$).

ncert-physics-ch11.title: NCERT Class 10 Physics — Chapter 11: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
ncert-physics-ch11.description: Curriculum mapping for refraction through prisms, atmospheric refraction, dispersion, spectrum formation, rainbow physics, and Tyndall scattering.
ncert-physics-ch11.body:
# NCERT Class 10 Physics Chapter 11

Covers the structure and defects of the human eye, refraction of light through a glass prism, dispersion of white light, atmospheric refraction (twinkling of stars, advance sunrise), and scattering of light (blue color of sky, red color at sunset).

angle-of-deviation.title: Angle of Deviation (D or δ)
angle-of-deviation.description: The angular difference between the forward trajectory of the incident light ray and the backward extension of the emergent ray after passing through a prism.

sources.name: NCERT Class 10 Science
sources.chapter: Chapter 11: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
sources.section: 11.2 Refraction of Light through a Prism

equations.meaning: Deviation D equals the sum of incidence angle i and emergence angle e minus prism angle A.

angle-of-deviation.body:
# Angle of Deviation (D)

In a triangular prism, because the two lateral refracting surfaces are not parallel, the emergent ray is bent towards the thicker base of the prism. The angle between the incident direction and the final emergent direction is termed the Angle of Deviation ($D$).

bar-magnet.title: Permanent Bar Magnet & Magnetic Field Lines
bar-magnet.description: Rectangular ferromagnetic bar magnet producing a permanent dipolar magnetic field with closed external field loops directing from North to South pole.

sources.name: NCERT Class 10 Science
sources.chapter: Chapter 12: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

equations.meaning: Magnetic field on the axial line of a short magnetic dipole.

bar-magnet.body:
# Permanent Bar Magnet

The permanent bar magnet serves as the standard pedagogical exemplar in NCERT Chapter 12 for demonstrating magnetic poles, drawing field lines using iron filings and compass plotting, and understanding non-intersecting field geometry.

convex-lens.title: Double Convex Lens (Converging Lens)
convex-lens.description: Transparent optical element bounded by two outwardly curved spherical surfaces that refracts parallel incident light rays to converge at a focal point.

equations.meaning: Lens Formula relating image distance v, object distance u, and focal length f.
Optical power of a lens in dioptres (D).

convex-lens.body:
# Double Convex Lens

Double convex lenses are the principal optical component in compound microscopes, astronomical telescopes, camera objectives, and corrective spectacles for hypermetropia (farsightedness).

convex-mirror.title: Convex Mirror (Diverging Spherical Mirror)
convex-mirror.description: Curved reflective mirror with an outwardly curved spherical reflecting surface that diverges incident parallel rays from a virtual principal focus behind the mirror.

sources.name: NCERT Class 10 Science
sources.section: 9.2 Reflection of Light by Spherical Mirrors

equations.meaning: Mirror Formula relating image distance v, object distance u, and focal length f.
Linear magnification formula (m < +1 for convex mirrors).

convex-mirror.body:
# Convex Mirror

A convex mirror is a diverging spherical mirror whose reflecting surface curves outward toward the light source. It forms virtual, erect, and diminished images for all real object positions. Because it curves outwards, it gathers light over a wide angle, offering drivers and shopkeepers a broad field of view.

electric-circuit.title: Electric Circuit & Ohm's Law Verification Setup
electric-circuit.description: Closed conducting loop comprising a DC power source, plug key switch, ammeter in series, voltmeter in parallel, rheostat, and nichrome resistor wire.

equations.meaning: Ohm's Law: Potential difference V across conductor equals electric current I multiplied by resistance R.
Resistance formula in terms of electrical resistivity rho, length l, and cross-sectional area A.

safety: Ensure key is inserted only while taking readings to prevent resistor heating and resistance drift.
electric-circuit.body:
# Electric Circuit & Ohm's Law Apparatus

Standard CBSE Class 10 electricity setup for verifying the linear $V-I$ characteristic of metallic conductors. By varying the position of the rheostat sliding contact, students record multiple current-voltage pairs to plot a straight-line graph through the origin, whose slope represents the ohmic resistance $R = \Delta V / \Delta I$.

electric-motor.title: Direct Current (DC) Electric Motor
electric-motor.description: Rotating electromechanical machine that converts direct current electrical energy into mechanical rotational kinetic energy using Fleming's Left-Hand Rule.

sources.name: NCERT Class 10 Science
sources.chapter: Chapter 12: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

equations.meaning: Lorentz magnetic force on current-carrying conductor arms AB and CD.
Electromagnetic torque rotating the armature coil.

electric-motor.body:
# Direct Current (DC) Electric Motor

The electric motor demonstrates the fundamental conversion of electrical energy to mechanical work. In CBSE Class 10 examinations, students are evaluated on diagram labelling (armature, split rings, brushes, field magnets) and explaining the function of the split-ring commutator in reversing current direction every half-turn to sustain continuous rotation.

galvanometer.title: Center-Zero Moving Coil Galvanometer
galvanometer.description: An electromechanical instrument used for detecting and indicating the presence and direction of minute electric currents in a circuit.

sources.name: NCERT Class 10 Science
sources.chapter: Chapter 12: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

equations.meaning: Deflection angle theta is directly proportional to current I passing through the moving coil.
Faraday's Law of induction generating current detected by galvanometer.

galvanometer.body:
# Galvanometer

The center-zero galvanometer is the essential detector in electromagnetic induction investigations. In NCERT Chapter 12 Activity 12.8, when the North pole of a bar magnet is thrust into a fixed coil of wire, the galvanometer needle undergoes a momentary deflection to one side, proving that motion relative to a magnetic field induces electrical current.

glass-prism-refraction.title: Refraction of Light Through a Triangular Glass Prism
glass-prism-refraction.description: Experimental demonstration of angular deviation and chromatic dispersion when a collimated light ray traverses non-parallel refracting boundaries of an optical prism.

sources.name: NCERT Class 10 Science

misconceptions.claim: Light passing through a prism behaves exactly like light passing through a rectangular glass slab.
misconceptions.correction: In a rectangular slab with parallel faces, light undergoes lateral displacement without angular deviation. In a prism with inclined faces, light undergoes net angular deviation (D).

glass-prism-refraction.body:
# Refraction of Light Through a Triangular Glass Prism

## 1. Pedagogical Overview
When a ray of light enters an equilateral triangular glass prism ($A = 60^\circ$):
1. **At first face $AB$ (Air $\rightarrow$ Glass)**: Light enters an optically denser medium ($n \approx 1.517$) and refracts towards the normal ($r_1 < i$).
2. **Inside the prism along $EF$**: The ray propagates through the bulk glass.
3. **At second face $AC$ (Glass $\rightarrow$ Air)**: Light exits into the optically rarer air and refracts away from the second normal ($e > r_2$).
4. **Deviation Angle ($D$)**: Extending the forward incident ray and backward emergent ray reveals the net angular deviation subtended at vertex $G$.

## 2. Planar Interface Ray Vector Dynamics
At each refracting boundary with outward surface normal $\mathbf{n}$ and incident ray direction unit vector $\mathbf{d}_1$:
- **Snell's Law in Vector Form**:
  $$\mathbf{d}_2 = \frac{n_1}{n_2}\mathbf{d}_1 + \left(\frac{n_1}{n_2}\cos\theta_1 - \cos\theta_2\right)\mathbf{n}$$
  where $\cos\theta_1 = -(\mathbf{d}_1 \cdot \mathbf{n})$ and $\cos\theta_2 = \sqrt{1 - \left(\frac{n_1}{n_2}\right)^2(1 - \cos^2\theta_1)}$.
- **Total Internal Reflection Boundary Check**:
  When transitioning from denser glass ($n_1 \approx 1.517$) to rarer air ($n_2 \approx 1.0$), the critical angle is $\theta_c = \arcsin(n_2 / n_1) \approx 41.2^\circ$. If the internal incidence angle $r_2 > \theta_c$, the radicand becomes negative; the transmitted refracted branch ceases to exist, and total internal reflection occurs.

optical-bench.body:
# Laboratory Optical Bench

The optical bench is the quintessential experimental apparatus used in secondary physics laboratories for verifying Snell's law, tracing conjugate foci, determining lens focal lengths, and observing image magnification transitions.

optical-dispersion.title: Dispersion of White Light into Spectrum (VIBGYOR)
optical-dispersion.description: The phenomenon of splitting composite polychromatic white light into its seven constituent spectral colors upon refraction through a dispersive medium.

sources.name: NCERT Class 10 Science
sources.chapter: Chapter 11: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
sources.section: 11.3 Dispersion of White Light by a Glass Prism

equations.meaning: Higher refractive index for shorter wavelengths leads to greater angular deviation.

misconceptions.claim: The prism creates color out of colorless light.
misconceptions.correction: White light already contains all spectral frequencies; the prism simply separates them spatially because their phase velocities in glass differ (dispersion).

optical-dispersion.body:
# Dispersion of White Light by a Glass Prism

Sir Isaac Newton was the first to demonstrate that sunlight consists of seven constituent colors by placing two identical prisms in an inverted combination to recombine the separated spectrum back into white light.
The dispersion arises because the speed of light $v$ in a material medium varies with wavelength $\lambda$ (Cauchy's dispersion equation: $n(\lambda) = A + B/\lambda^2$).

# Equilateral Triangular Glass Prism

A solid homogeneous block of optical glass (such as Schott N-BK7 crown glass) with two equilateral triangular end-faces and three rectangular lateral faces that refract and disperse light rays.

snells-law.title: Snell's Law of Refraction
snells-law.description: Fundamental optical law defining the invariant ratio between the sine of the angle of incidence and the sine of the angle of refraction across two isotropic media.

equations.meaning: Snell's Law expressing refractive index n21 in terms of incident angle i, refracted angle r, and phase velocities v1 and v2.

snells-law.body:
# Snell's Law of Refraction

The refractive index $n$ quantifies the factor by which light wavefronts slow down when entering an optically denser medium. 
For crown glass in air, $n \approx 1.517$, meaning light travels approximately $1.517\times$ slower in glass ($v \approx 1.98 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$) than in air/vacuum.

solenoid.title: Helical Solenoid with Uniform Axial Magnetic Field
solenoid.description: A long cylindrical coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire that produces a strong, uniform magnetic field inside when carrying electric current.

sources.name: NCERT Class 10 Science
sources.chapter: Chapter 12: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current
sources.section: 12.2.3 Magnetic Field due to a Current in a Solenoid

equations.meaning: Magnetic field inside an ideal solenoid where n = N/L (turns per unit length) and I is current.

solenoid.body:
# Solenoid

A solenoid consists of a helical winding of copper wire around an insulating or soft iron core. When an electric current flows through the coil, individual loop magnetic fields constructively interfere to produce a dense, uniform magnetic flux along the central axis.
